context.full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.
context.conclusion: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W⊂V_K invariant under ρ_K(x⊗1), ρ_K(y⊗1), and ρ_K(h⊗1), either W={0} or W=V_K. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module, for every field K and every prime p and integer 0≤λ<p, including λ=0 and p=2.

record.type: family of elements of U(sl₂(ℂ)) and their induced operators on V, indexed by nonnegative integers
record.definition: For every integer r≥0, X(r)=X_r=x^r/r! in the complex universal enveloping algebra U(sl₂(ℂ)); the same notation denotes its action on V. Powers are compositions on V, with zeroth power the identity.

record.type: family of elements of U(sl₂(ℂ)) and their induced operators on V, indexed by nonnegative integers
record.definition: For every integer r≥0, Y(r)=Y_r=y^r/r! in U(sl₂(ℂ)); the same notation denotes its action on V, with zeroth power the identity.
U_Z is the unital ℤ-subalgebra of U(sl₂(ℂ)) generated by X(r) and Y(r) for all integers r≥0, acting on V by its given sl₂(ℂ)-representation.

record.type: p-local subring of ℚ, with its usual inclusion in ℂ
record.definition: R=ℤ_(p)={a/b∈ℚ:a,b∈ℤ, b≠0, p∤b}, with the operations inherited from ℚ and its usual embedding in ℂ.
M_R=R⊗_ℤ M. Its elementary tensors are written r⊗m with r∈R and m∈M.
ι_M(r⊗m)=r m, extending by addition from pure tensors, where R⊂ℂ and M⊂V. When its injectivity has been proved we identify M_R with its image under ι_M.
For i,j∈I, E_ij=E(i,j) is the unique complex-linear operator sending e_j to e_i and e_k to zero for each k∈I with k≠j.
Π=Y(λ)X(λ), with rightmost factor applied first.

record.type: family of R-submodules of ℂ indexed by I
record.definition: For i∈I, J_i={c∈ℂ:c e_i∈ι_M(M_R)}. Scalar operations are inherited from ℂ.
V_K=V(K)=M⊗_ℤ K, with K acting on the second tensor factor.

record.type: K-vector space obtained from the Chevalley integer form
record.definition: L_K=L(K)=(ℤx+ℤy+ℤh)⊗_ℤ K. The integer span uses the Chevalley generators in sl₂(ℂ) and its inherited bracket, and scalar extension gives the bracket on L_K.
For t∈ℤx+ℤy+ℤh, c,d∈K and m∈M, ρ_K(t⊗c)(m⊗d)=(tm)⊗(cd), extended additively and K-linearly. On V_K the words invariant under x,y,h mean invariant under ρ_K(x⊗1), ρ_K(y⊗1), ρ_K(h⊗1).
F_p=ℤ/pℤ, with residue classes of integers and quotient ring operations; its canonical map into K is [a]↦a·1_K.

record.statement: n=λ+1>0 and |I|=n. The vectors (e_i)_(i∈I) form a complex basis of V. For every integer t≥0, h y^t v=(λ−2t)y^t v, and for t≥1, x y^t v=t(λ−t+1)y^(t−1)v. Moreover y^(λ+1)v=0 and all higher powers on v vanish. Their action matrices are x e_0=0, x e_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1) for 1≤i≤λ; y e_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for 0≤i<λ, y e_λ=0; h e_i=(λ−2i)e_i for i∈I. For every integer r≥0 and i∈I, X(r)e_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_(i−r) if r≤i and zero otherwise; Y(r)e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤λ and zero otherwise. Each displayed nonzero coefficient is an integer. Here binom(a,r)=a!/(r!(a−r)!) for integers 0≤r≤a; these are the usual integer binomial coefficients.

R is the subring ℤ_(p) of ℚ⊂ℂ. The map ι_M:R⊗_ℤ M→V is injective. With M_R identified with its image it is a free R-module with an R-basis of n elements and its complex span is V. Each X(r),Y(r), r≥0, preserves M and M_R. The operators x,y,h preserve M; ℤx+ℤy+ℤh is closed under the Lie bracket. For t∈ℤx+ℤy+ℤh, m∈M and c,d∈K, the rule (t⊗c)(m⊗d)=tm⊗(cd) is well-defined on (ℤx+ℤy+ℤh)⊗_ℤ K and V_K=M⊗_ℤ K and defines a K-linear Lie action. For every integer 0≤r≤λ, p∤r!, so r! is a unit in R. For all i,j∈I, binom(λ,j) is a unit in R and Π=E_λλ, X(λ−i)Π=E_iλ, ΠY(λ−j)=binom(λ,j)E_λj, and E_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1)X(λ−i)ΠY(λ−j). Consequently all E_ij preserve M_R.

record.statement: All J_i for i∈I are the same nonzero finitely generated R-submodule J⊂ℂ. Under ι_M, M_R=⊕_(i∈I) J e_i: the map γ↦Σ_(i∈I)γ(i)e_i is an R-linear bijection J^I→M_R. The multiplication map μ:ℚ⊗_R J→ℂ, μ(q⊗c)=qc, is injective with image the rational span of J, and dim_ℚ(ℚ⊗_R J)=1. There exists b∈J with b≠0 and J=Rb; for every such b the vectors (b e_i)_(i∈I) form an R-basis of M_R.

binders.type: map ℚ⊗_R J→ℂ defined by μ(q⊗c)=qc

record.statement: The integer map extends to a ring map R→K. For every pair of integers A₀,B₀ with B₀≠0 and p∤B₀ it sends A₀/B₀ to (A₀·1_K)(B₀·1_K)^(-1). Also R/pR≅F_p via the residue of A₀/B₀↦[A₀][B₀]^(-1). There are K-linear isomorphisms Γ:V_K→M_R⊗_R K and Δ:M_R⊗_R K→(M_R/pM_R)⊗_(F_p)K. They satisfy Γ(m⊗c)=(1⊗m)⊗c, Γ^(-1)((r⊗m)⊗c)=m⊗(r̄c), Δ(z⊗c)=[z]⊗c, and Δ^(-1)([z]⊗c)=z⊗c, where r̄ denotes the image of r in K. They intertwine induced lattice operators. There exist b∈J\{0} with J=Rb and a family β:I→V_K such that β_i=Γ^(-1)((b e_i)⊗1) for i∈I and β is a K-basis of V_K; here b e_i is regarded as the unique element of M_R mapping to that vector by ι_M. In particular dim_K(V_K)=n>0. Write a=ρ_K(x⊗1), d=ρ_K(y⊗1), t=ρ_K(h⊗1). On this basis aβ_0=0, aβ_i=(λ−i+1)β_(i−1) for i≥1; dβ_i=(i+1)β_(i+1) for i<λ and dβ_λ=0; tβ_i=(λ−2i)β_i. All integers in these formulas are mapped into K. For every integer s with 0≤s≤λ, s!≠0 in K and the lattice-induced X(s),Y(s) on V_K equal (s!)^(-1)a^s and (s!)^(-1)d^s. For i,j∈I let T_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1)((λ−i)!)^(-1)a^(λ−i) (λ!)^(-1)d^λ (λ!)^(-1)a^λ ((λ−j)!)^(-1)d^(λ−j), with rightmost operator applied first and all scalar factors in K. Then binom(λ,j)≠0 in K and T_ij β_k=β_i when k=j and zero when k≠j. Thus T_ij are the coordinate matrix units for this K-basis.
